items.title: Generally Available: Managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway for AKS
items.description:
AKS will now provision and manage a StandardV2 NAT Gateway for clusters using an AKS-managed virtual network.

StandardV2 is now the default managed NAT Gateway SKU for new clusters in supported regions when using the managedNATGateway outbound type. StandardV2 NAT Gateway provides zone redundancy by default, higher bandwidth and throughput, and IPv6 support.

Existing AKS clusters can migrate from a managed Standard NAT Gateway or load balancer to a managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway.

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028
items.description:
Microsoft Dev Box will retire on September 18, 2028. Beginning on September 14, 2026, Microsoft Dev Box will begin the closing-down process. After retirement, Microsoft Dev Box will no longer be available. 

Microsoft Dev Box is currently in maintenance mode, and Microsoft’s investments for developer cloud environments are focused on Windows 365. Existing Microsoft Dev Box usage remains supported during the transition period, and we recommend that you begin planning your migration now to avoid disruption to developer workflows. 

What this means for you 

  • If you currently use Microsoft Dev Box, you can continue using your existing deployments during the transition period. 
  • No new feature development is planned for the service. 
  • You should evaluate and begin planning your move to Windows 365, which is the recommended path forward for virtualized developer environments. 

Recommended action 

  • Review your current Dev Box usage, including dev centers, projects, pools, images, and developer workflows. 
  • Identify which scenarios can transition directly to Windows 365 and which require additional planning. 
  • Validate identity, device management, networking, image, and licensing requirements for your future-state environment. 
  • Begin testing replacement workflows as early as possible to reduce risk before retirement.  

If you have questions or need support, please contact your Microsoft representative.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Deployment Environments will be retired on February 22, 2027
items.description:
Azure Deployment Environments will retire on February 22, 2027. Beginning on September 14, 2026, Azure Deployment Environments will begin the closing-down process. After retirement, the service will no longer be available. 

To help avoid disruption, we recommend that you begin assessing your current usage and planning your transition now. Review the environments, templates, and workflows in your organization that depend on Azure Deployment Environments and identify the replacement approach that best supports your requirements. 

What this means for you 

  • You should review all current Azure Deployment Environments usage across subscriptions, projects, templates, and deployment workflows. 
  • You should identify an alternative approach for environment provisioning and developer self-service before the retirement date. 
  • You should begin validating your migration plan as early as possible to minimize operational and development impact. 

Recommended action 

  • Inventory your current environments, templates, catalogs, and provisioning workflows. 
  • Determine the target platform or service that will replace Azure Deployment Environments for your organization. 
  • Test your migration path, including governance, access control, infrastructure-as-code compatibility, and developer workflow readiness. 
  • Communicate internal timelines to platform engineering teams, developers, and administrators.

items.title: Generally Available: Exceptions in WAF for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door
items.description:
Announcing the general availability of exceptions for Web Application Firewall on Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door.

Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) helps protect your web applications from common threats and attacks. In some cases, WAF may block requests that are safe and expected for your application. Existing exclusions help reduce false positives by omitting specific request attributes, such as headers, cookies, query string arguments, or body fields, from WAF evaluation while the rest of the request continues to be inspected. 

Exceptions provide additional flexibility by allowing specific requests to bypass WAF inspection at the rule, rule group, or managed ruleset level. Exceptions can be defined using request URI, remote IP address, or request header name and value, helping customers tune WAF policies more precisely while keeping other protections active. 

To configure exceptions, navigate to your WAF policy in the Azure portal, select Managed rules, and then add an exception. 

Learn more: 

  • Application Gateway documentation 
  • Front Door documentation

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management
items.description:
The integration between Microsoft Agent 365 and Azure API Management is now available in public preview, helping organizations connect centralized governance with runtime enforcement for MCP servers and tools.

With this integration, organizations can:

  • Discover Azure API Management gateways and MCP servers in Agent 365, creating a centralized inventory of gateway-managed tools.

  • Control access to MCP servers from Agent 365, with enforcement applied by Azure API Management at runtime.

  • Apply tool-level access controls with the Azure API Management AI Gateway tier, including blocking individual tools without disabling the entire MCP server.

  • Monitor tool activity to support auditing, operational visibility, and incident investigation.

  • Protect tool interactions using Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Purview capabilities to evaluate tool requests and responses for security threats and sensitive-information risks.

Azure API Management v2 tiers support centralized MCP inventory and server-level blocking and unblocking. The AI Gateway tier, currently in preview, adds individual tool-level blocking, tool activity observability, and tool threat protection.

This integration enables AI administrators to manage governance centrally in Agent 365 while platform teams enforce those policies through Azure API Management in the customer’s Azure environment.

items.title: Announcing: Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace expands to Hong Kong
items.description: Multiparty private offers give Microsoft partners a way to procure third-party cloud and AI solutions for customers through Marketplace. Software companies can expand into new markets by working with partners that bring established customer relationships, while customers rely on their trusted partners to manage their cloud and AI initiatives.
